record.original_question: Is it true that a non-spreading homeomorphism of the 2-torus has conjugates arbitrarily close to a rotation ?

evidence.quote: Question 7.7. Is it true that a non-spreading homeomorphism of the 2-torus has conjugates arbitrarily close to a rotation ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ be the 2-torus, and let $\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$ denote the group of homeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^2$ that are isotopic to the identity, endowed with the uniform (compact-open) topology. A homeomorphism $f \in \mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$ is said to be non-spreading if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that, for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and every set $E \subset \mathbb{T}^2$ of diameter at most $\delta$ (measured with respect to a fixed Riemannian distance), the iterate $f^n(E)$ has diameter at most $\varepsilon$.

A rotation of $\mathbb{T}^2$ is a map of the form $R_\alpha(x) = x + \alpha \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^2}$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^2$.

Question: Is it true that for every non-spreading homeomorphism $f$ of $\mathbb{T}^2$, the closure of the conjugacy class
$$\{ h \circ f \circ h^{-1} : h \in \mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2) \}$$
in $\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$ contains a rotation? Equivalently, can $f$ be conjugated to maps arbitrarily close to some rotation $R_\alpha$ in the uniform topology?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a recent problem list (2025) on foliations and diffeomorphism groups and is stated as an open question. Related results are known: for closed surfaces of genus at least 2, the closure of the conjugacy class of any non-spreading homeomorphism contains the identity; for surfaces with boundary (other than disc, annulus, Möbius strip), similar results hold. For the 2-torus the analogous statement (with rotations replacing the identity) remains an open conjecture, supported by partial results in pseudo-rotation theory.

status_evidence.title: Rotation theory of torus homeomorphisms II
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses pseudo-rotations of the torus and their conjugacy properties.
status_evidence.claim: Pseudo-rotations of the torus and related conjugacy/closure problems are an active topic.

status_evidence.title: On Torus Homeomorphisms Semiconjugate to irrational Rotations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when torus homeomorphisms are semiconjugate to irrational rotations.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results on conjugacy/semiconjugacy to rotations exist but do not resolve the question for non-spreading homeomorphisms of the 2-torus.
